newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-CONFIDENT DUTCH GIVE BELGIUM A HELPING HAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONFIDENT DUTCH GIVE BELGIUM A HELPING HAND.

text.p: Ever-confident Netherlands did Belgium the biggest possible favour by forcing them into their familiar role of underdogs before their crucial World Cup qualifier on Saturday.
The Dutch donned the mantle of European group seven favourites after thrashing Wales 7-1 last month.
Self-assured comments by coach Guus Hiddink and his squad underlined the situation.
"We always go for victory," Hiddink said.
"There's absolutely no reason to be afraid. We should be able to beat Belgium," said defender Frank de Boer. "The Netherlands are better," said Jaap Stam.
History proves them right with the Dutch having won 53 of their 117 previous games, against 39 for Belgium.
Hiddink said it was in the Dutch nature to attack and try to dominate their opponents. Belgium use a different approach.
They often have trouble imposing their game on weaker opponents and struggled to beat Turkey and San Marino in their previous two qualifiers.
But Belgium are dangerous when they can rely on a solid defensive bloc and apply counter-attacking tactics.
"I'm expecting a lot of Belgians in the back. The emphasis is on defence. There might be five defenders," Hiddink said.
But he dismissed remarks by his Belgian counterpart Wilfried Van Moer that many Belgian players had an inferiority complex.
"I don't buy that," said Hiddink who sees Saturday's game as the first real test for the Dutch after two comfortable wins against Wales.
"Belgium is in an entirely different category," he said.
Ajax striker Patrick Kluivert, drafted for his first international since Euro 96, said the Dutch did not underestimate Belgium.
"But we always go for victory. Call it Amsterdam bluff or whatever, but we're only coming to Brussels to win," he said.
But Belgium's midfielder Lorenzo Staelens noted the Dutch were also rated three times better than Belgium ahead of their previous encounter in the first round of the 1994 World Cup.
Belgium won 1-0.
Hiddink noted his team could afford to draw in Brussels as it would be difficult for Belgium and outsiders Turkey to improve on the Dutch goal difference.
Dutchmen Ronald de Boer and striker Dennis Bergkamp are still dogged by knee and thigh problems respectively but both were expected to start the game and complete the line-up which routed Wales.
On the Belgian side, captain Enzo Scifo is unavailable because of a toe injury.
But striker Marc Wilmots, who was at loggerheads with Van Moer's predecessor Paul Van Himst and quit after the 1994 World Cup finals, is back in business.
So is Newcastle defender Philippe Albert, who had been ignored by Van Moer for the two previous qualifiers.
Teams (probable):
Belgium - Filip De Wilde, Philippe Albert, Bertrand Crasson, Eric Van Meir, Pascal Renier, Philippe Leonard, Lorenzo Staelens, Marc Degryse, Marc Wilmots, Luc Nilis, Luis Oliveira.
Netherlands - Edwin van der Sar, Michael Reiziger, Jaap Stam, Frank de Boer, Arthur Numan, Aron Winter, Wim Jonk, Clarence Seedorf, Phillip Cocu, Ronald de Boer, Dennis Bergkamp.
